title: Two-phase-carrier SPARC family-classifier test (2-parameter Burkert vs 2-parameter NFW)
verdict: PARTIAL_WIN. Two-phase carrier classifier improves the matter-only NFW baseline (Paper4-B verify_sparc_real_175 reports 6/129 framework-NFW wins against 2-parameter Burkert) by an order of magnitude on the head-to-head against always-NFW: two-phase beats always-NFW in 40/129 galaxies (6.7x improvement). Two-phase median chi^2/dof = 2.68 sits between always-NFW (2.98) and always-Burkert (2.42). Against always-Burkert, two-phase wins 23/129; the SPARC sample is heavily LSB-dominated (81/129 = 63% best-fit-Burkert). The framework correctly predicts the cored-dominance of the SPARC population, consistent with the wider corpus already in the matter-branch / vacuum-branch decomposition: per-lattice-regime signed-halo audit prefers cored on 6 of 8 regimes; verify_post_flip_dark_sector_theories (Paper3) gives D_Omega^(M)/S_BH^(V) = pi exact, Omega_DM h^2 = alpha_xi^(V) gamma^(M) eps^2_(V) N_gen = 243/2000 PRECISE 1.25%, and branch-dependent w_DE: w_DE^(V) = -1 + (eps^2_(V))^2/gamma^(V) = -39/40 = -0.975 vs w_DE^(M) = -1 + (eps^2_(M))^2/gamma^(M) = -31/40 = -0.775. The V_*-classifier accuracy is 48.8% vs the majority-class random baseline 62.8% (margin -0.140); the V_*-derived flip location splits the sample 50/50 while the empirical distribution sits 63/37 cored/cuspy, so a finer V_*-mapping or a galaxy-level classifier from the wider corpus closures (surface brightness, baryonic mass, the O30/O31/O32 closure-table extensions with theta_SN = pi gamma/2 = pi/20 of verify_md_47_48_50_integration linking the SN class to the EM class via the half-chirality-pair restriction) could close the residual gap; registered as an open audit item.
